install: Normal upstream install: `squeez update` (downloads the latest release, checks checksums.sha256, swaps the running exe by rename, refreshes Claude Code hooks), then `squeez setup --host=<h>` for each safe host.

overlays.what: Owner OpenCode plugin: on Windows the wrapper follows the OpenCode `shell` config key, not the OS. A PowerShell shell gets powershell.exe -EncodedCommand (upstream wraps with POSIX quoting and squeez wrap runs them in bash) and WSL commands bounded by a taskkill /F /T supervisor that exits 124; a bash shell gets the POSIX form with a forward-slash quoted binary path, and WSL commands are left unwrapped so the host timeout bounds them. The plugin starts no child process synchronously: inside the OpenCode server the first execSync of a hook call fails at once with a false ETIMEDOUT, which dropped the read/grep budget; it uses existsSync and async execFile (one retry, 60 s cache). Post-execution tracking pipes a JSON payload to `squeez track-result` over stdin with EOF (the observer no-ops on empty stdin — upstream #247); the v2 path subscribes shell.exited for shell completions and session.execution.started (per-session dedupe) for init.

overlays.retireWhen: A squeez release's opencode-plugin/squeez.js contains the -EncodedCommand wrapping chosen by the OpenCode shell, a bounded WSL timeout, no execSync/execFileSync/spawnSync (#245), the v2 setup(ctx) entry (#242) and the #247 event-surface fixes (marker: shell_status in the plugin) (check by marker, not by changelog). The #242 dual export was merged into this file on 2026-10-02 (see overlay opencode-plugin-v2).

overlays.what: The same merged plugin installed to the OpenCode v2 profile as a config-dir drop. One file, two entry points: server() for v1 and setup(ctx) for v2 — the v2 path registers on ctx.shell/ctx.tool/ctx.event with the wrapper following the shell each create.before event carries (#244), no synchronous spawns (#245/#246), async budget injection with a 60 s cache, and the WSL supervisor on PowerShell shells (#239). This is the migration-dossier §3.6 merge of PR #242's dual export with the owner overlays. It also tracks shell completions via the shell.exited bus event with a real stdin payload (track-result was a silent no-op on empty stdin everywhere) and restores per-session init via the session.execution.started alias with per-session dedupe (#247, PR #242 commit 4d2a0f3); v2 execute.after is restricted to read/grep/glob so shell is never double-counted.

configWhy.context_window_tokens: owner pin at 1M so squeez's context meter matches the model window
configWhy.auto_compress_md: owner policy X-28/X-98/X-119: compress-md rewrote CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md on every session start; each host's init reads its own config.ini, and setup creates new host configs with true
configWhy.configRequiredWhen: a missing config.ini is not neutral: init falls back to Config::default() (init.rs load_config_from), whose auto_compress_md is true (config.rs), so a host whose init trigger exists must have its file. The OpenCode v2 profile (XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/.opencode-v2/config) reads ~/.opencode-v2/config/opencode/squeez/config.ini, which was absent until 2026-09-30

omoClaudeHooksOff.why: oh-my-openagent runs Claude Code PreToolUse hooks on OpenCode tool calls and applies updatedInput with output.args = {...} (packages/utils/src/replace-tool-args.ts). OpenCode executes the original args object (session/tools.ts passes { args } and never reads output.args back), so the Claude hook's wrap is dropped and the squeez plugin, which runs after OMO, edits the detached copy: commands ran raw except the ones squeez should-wrap rejects. Under OpenCode the squeez plugin is the wrapper, so squeez's Claude pretooluse.sh is excluded for OMO. OMO matches the pattern against command.split('/').pop(), which for the registered command is pretooluse.sh followed by a double quote. OMO's non-interactive-env hook detached every command containing the word git the same way; that half is OMO ledger fix 17-tool-args-in-place (oh-my-openagent-fix/local-fixes, 2026-10-02), which makes OMO edit the args in place. With it the Claude hook's rewrite would take effect too, but it only emits the POSIX form (wrong for a PowerShell shell) and also compresses Task prompts, so the exclusion stays and the shell-aware plugin is the only wrapper under OpenCode. Remove only with an owner decision on which wrapper should run.
